name: Hearth
description: Hearth brings your services, your infrastructure, and an AI administrator together in one place. Ember, its AI, looks after your homelab with you: it investigates, explains, and fixes things through plans you approve.
status: In active development. Not available to download yet.

emberLoop.note: Talk or type, in plain words.
Reads logs, app status, and your machine through Hearth's own tools.
Explains what is wrong and how sure it is.
Proposes an exact plan, step by step.
Nothing changes until you approve that exact plan.
Installs, restarts, repairs, and settings in any connected app, through plans you approve.
Every change is checked afterwards, and undone on its own if it fails.
Keeps what it learned, with you reviewing what it saves.

screens.title: Home
screens.caption: Ember in the middle, your active projects around it, what needs you in one row, and your homelab's vital signs below. All on one screen.

screens.title: Ember goes where you go
screens.caption: Ember's chat stays open as you move between pages, so you can keep talking while you check a service or a setting.

screens.title: The Lair: a panel for each app
screens.caption: Open any app beside Ember. qBittorrent shows stalled and broken torrents first, each with the repairs that fit it.

screens.title: Sonarr, explained
screens.caption: Stuck and failed downloads named with the app's own reason, and one-click Import or Search, each a plan you approve.

screens.title: Who is watching what
screens.caption: Plex libraries and live streams: direct play or transcode, buffering, and an Ask Ember button on every stream.

screens.title: Invite friends and family
screens.caption: Create Wizarr invitations, choose libraries and how long access lasts, and see who has used them, without leaving Hearth.

screens.title: Storage & Files
screens.caption: Every drive with its health and temperature, plus files, recent downloads, file journeys, and RAID arrays.

screens.title: The War Room
screens.caption: Your projects with Claude Code, Codex, or a local Ollama model: a terminal, a task queue, files, and a kill switch.

screens.title: Notifications
screens.caption: Email, Discord, ntfy, or a webhook. Hearth writes only when something matters and says whether you need to act.

screens.title: Tell friends what is new
screens.caption: When a movie or show lands in Plex or Jellyfin, Hearth posts it to your friends' Discord with its details and trailer. Here, Spider-Man: Brand New Day.

screens.title: Watch parties
screens.caption: Pick a movie and a time, add a note and where to watch, and Hearth posts the invitation with reminders. Friends answer I'm in or Can't make it.

screens.title: Planned, with a guest list
screens.caption: The watch party, who is coming, and spots left. Change the time, add a room code, or cancel it, and everyone invited hears about it.

screens.title: Add Discord in one click
screens.caption: Add a destination, choose the Hearth bot, and pick who reads it. A friends and family channel only ever gets media announcements, never system alerts.

screens.title: The Hearth bot, no token needed
screens.caption: Add Hearth to your Discord server, pick the channel, and you are done. Movie night invitations get I'm in and Can't make it buttons.

screens.title: Or use your own Discord bot
screens.caption: Prefer your own? Set it up step by step in about two minutes. Its token goes into Hearth's vault and is never shown again.

screens.title: Make Ember your own
screens.caption: Rename your AI, pick a built-in voice or your own speech machine, and choose how much it may do on its own.

screens.title: Plan your first homelab
screens.caption: Pick what sounds fun in plain words. Hearth looks at your computer, only if you say yes, and explains every option.

screens.title: A plan that fits your computer
screens.caption: Every app explained: what it does, why it was picked, what it costs, and whether it runs comfortably on your machine.

screens.title: You approve the exact plan
screens.caption: Each step says how it will be checked and what happens if a later step fails. Approval covers this plan, once.
